headline: High: Plane’s broad network egress and file uploads create default data-leak and compliance risk when paired with the docs-only audio agent; prompt-injection and conflict risks are lower.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: A has no documented I/O surfaces beyond docs-only metadata, while B accepts file uploads and can call external APIs. There is no documented shared channel or parser bridge between ai-engineering-hub and Plane, so prompt injection is not default-path dangerous; the only plausible bridge is manual content transfer or uploaded files.
conditions: IF an operator copies A-generated text into a Plane issue or file upload, then injected instructions can reach B.
IF Plane is configured to parse uploaded content as task instructions, then malicious content from A can influence B.
mitigations: Disable copy-paste of untrusted A output into Plane tasks.
Require a human review step before any Plane import from A.
Use a fixed template for uploads that strips instruction-like text.
Tag imported content as untrusted in Plane descriptions.
requires-engineering: add provenance labels on imported artifacts.

B_data_leakage.rationale: B has broad network egress and file uploads, so any sensitive material placed into Plane can leave the local boundary by default. A is docs-only and touches no data classes, so it is not itself a sensitive source; however, the pair still creates a leakage path if A-derived content or operator data is uploaded into B.
conditions: IF A-derived notes, files, or transcripts are uploaded into Plane, then B can transmit them off-host.
IF Plane is deployed with its documented API integrations enabled, then uploaded content may flow to third parties.
mitigations: Avoid uploading sensitive artifacts into Plane.
Restrict Plane integrations to an allowlist.
Use a redaction pass before file upload.
Store sensitive A outputs outside Plane.
requires-engineering: enforce DLP on Plane uploads.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: A is not runnable and exposes no write surfaces, while B explicitly has write_filesystem=false and supports multiple instances. That makes overlapping write conflict unlikely; the main remaining risk is operational confusion, not concurrent mutation of shared state.
conditions: IF B is deployed with an external writable mount not reflected in its profile, then write conflicts could emerge.
IF an operator manually synchronizes artifacts between A and B, then stale-state conflicts may occur.
mitigations: Keep A and B on separate workspaces.
Do not mount a shared writable directory.
Use read-only exports from A into B.
Document a single source of truth for tasks.
requires-engineering: add locking if shared storage is introduced.

D_cascading_error.rationale: B handles issues, tasks, and roadmaps and can act on uploaded files and hyperlinks, so A-generated content could be treated as authoritative if manually transferred. A is docs-only and not runnable, which lowers direct automation risk, but the pair still supports a human-in-the-loop cascade from A output into B work products.
conditions: IF A-generated summaries are pasted into Plane without verification, then B may propagate errors into issues or roadmaps.
IF Plane automation is configured to create tasks from uploaded content, then unverified A output can cascade downstream.
mitigations: Require source links on every imported item.
Verify A outputs against originals before creating Plane tasks.
Mark imported summaries as provisional.
Limit automation to reviewed items only.
requires-engineering: add validation rules for imported content.

E_compliance.rationale: B stores issues, tasks, files, images, hyperlinks, and notes and can egress broadly, while A is docs-only and touches no regulated data classes. The pair is not a clear residency violation by itself, but Plane’s default cloud-style handling can create retention and transfer mismatches if operators place regulated content into it.
conditions: IF regulated data is entered into Plane, then retention and transfer controls must match that data class.
IF Plane is used for EU personal data without a DPA or residency controls, then compliance risk increases.
mitigations: Do not store regulated data in Plane.
Review Plane retention settings before use.
Limit API integrations for regulated projects.
Separate regulated and non-regulated workspaces.
requires-engineering: add residency and retention enforcement.
